package_info.package_versions: versions vulnerable to CVE-2021-30116 (exact versions not specified in report)
package_info.why_malicious: Kaseya VSA (on-premises) was exploited via a zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2021-30116) that allowed unauthenticated attackers to bypass authentication and execute arbitrary commands on the VSA server. This enabled mass deployment of ransomware to all endpoints managed by the compromised VSA instance. The software itself was not maliciously altered, but its legitimate remote management and scripting features were abused to facilitate a large-scale ransomware attack.

execution_context.trigger: remote exploit (pre-authentication remote code execution) via zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2021-30116)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Arbitrary command execution via CVE-2021-30116 (details not disclosed in report; involves unauthenticated attackers sending specially crafted HTTP requests to the VSA server, triggering execution of attacker-supplied commands on managed endpoints through VSA's scripting engine).
malicious_snippets.code_language: unknown (likely shell, PowerShell, or batch commands executed via VSA's scripting capabilities)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Enables attackers to bypass authentication and remotely execute arbitrary commands on all endpoints managed by the compromised VSA server, leveraging VSA's legitimate remote management and scripting features.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unauthenticated remote command execution in enterprise management software is a critical security risk, as it allows attackers to control all managed endpoints without any legitimate credentials.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior: Only authenticated, authorized administrators can execute scripts or commands on endpoints via VSA. Malicious behavior: Attackers can execute arbitrary commands on all endpoints without authentication, using crafted requests.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use would be authenticated administrators deploying scripts, updates, or configuration changes to managed endpoints for IT maintenance.
key_indicators: pre-authentication remote code execution via VSA web interface
abuse of VSA's remote management scripting features for unauthorized command execution
sudden execution of commands/scripts across multiple endpoints without corresponding admin activity
unusual or unauthorized HTTP requests to VSA server endpoints associated with scripting or command execution

execution_context.trigger: post-exploitation (after gaining RCE on VSA server via CVE-2021-30116)
execution_context.file_location: deployed to all managed endpoints via VSA's scripting or payload deployment mechanism

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Ransomware payload (exact code not disclosed; typically involves VSA deploying and executing a ransomware binary on each managed endpoint, which encrypts files and displays a ransom note).
malicious_snippets.code_language: binary executable (likely Windows PE format; deployment may use PowerShell or batch scripts)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Encrypts files on victim endpoints and displays a ransom note demanding payment for decryption, resulting in widespread operational disruption.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Mass deployment of ransomware to all managed endpoints via IT management software is highly anomalous and destructive, indicating abuse of privileged access.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior: VSA is used to deploy legitimate software updates, patches, or IT scripts to endpoints. Malicious behavior: VSA is used to distribute and execute ransomware, causing simultaneous file encryption and ransom demands across the network.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use would be mass deployment of security patches, software updates, or IT automation scripts to endpoints by authorized administrators.
key_indicators: simultaneous execution of ransomware binaries across many endpoints managed by the same VSA instance
use of VSA's scripting or file distribution features to deploy non-standard or unsigned binaries
appearance of ransom note files on multiple endpoints within a short time window
unexpected encryption of files on endpoints following VSA-initiated actions

attack_chain.action: Attacker exploits zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2021-30116) to gain unauthenticated remote code execution on the Kaseya VSA server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker obtains the ability to execute arbitrary commands on all endpoints managed by the compromised VSA server.

attack_chain.action: Attacker leverages VSA's remote management and scripting features to deploy and execute ransomware payloads on all downstream managed endpoints.
attack_chain.leads_to: Mass ransomware infection and file encryption across customer networks, resulting in operational disruption and ransom demands.

behavioral_signatures: Unauthenticated remote command execution attempts against the VSA server, especially via HTTP requests to scripting or command execution endpoints
Mass deployment of identical scripts or binaries to all managed endpoints within a short time window, not initiated by known administrators
Simultaneous ransomware activity (file encryption, ransom note creation) across multiple endpoints managed by the same VSA instance
Unusual or unauthorized use of VSA's scripting or file distribution features
file_indicators: Unexpected scripts or binaries deployed via VSA's scripting or file distribution features (e.g., files not matching known-good hashes or not previously seen in environment)
Presence of known ransomware binaries or their variants on endpoints (e.g., REvil/Sodinokibi payloads)
Ransom note files (e.g., README.txt, HOW-TO-DECRYPT.txt) appearing on multiple endpoints simultaneously
Newly created or modified files with extensions commonly used by ransomware (e.g., .encrypted, .locked)
network_indicators: Unusual outbound connections from the VSA server to external, attacker-controlled infrastructure (e.g., C2 servers, dropzones)
Spike in network traffic between the VSA server and all managed endpoints during the attack window
Possible command and control (C2) traffic from endpoints post-infection, including attempts to contact known ransomware infrastructure
Unexpected inbound HTTP requests to VSA server endpoints associated with scripting or command execution, especially from unfamiliar IP addresses
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor VSA server logs for unauthenticated or anomalous HTTP requests, especially those triggering command execution or scripting features. Alert on mass deployment of new scripts or binaries via VSA, particularly if not initiated by authorized administrators. Correlate simultaneous ransomware activity (file encryption, ransom note creation) across endpoints managed by the same VSA instance. Scan endpoints for known ransomware binaries, ransom notes, and unusual file extensions. Monitor network traffic for spikes between VSA server and endpoints, and for outbound connections to known malicious infrastructure. Review VSA administrative activity logs for signs of privilege escalation or unauthorized actions.
